speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle and now present with increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or fever accompanying your joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (left ankle, now right knee), urethritis (pain with urination), and a young male patient with recent sexual activity and inconsistent condom use is highly suggestive of this condition. I will order a Urinalysis and request images of the right knee to confirm the diagnosis.
